newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Corpoven revenues up 35 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Corpoven revenues up 35 pct in 1996.

text.p: Corpoven, subsidiary of Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), saw its income jump by 35 percent in 1996 to $6.56 billion on a production capacity growth of 12 percent to 1.063 million barrels per day (bpd), the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
The huge revenue growth coincided with a 20 percent rise in world oil prices during the period.
Corpoven chairman Guillermo Archcila said the results were the best in the company's history, producing a 1.468 trillion bolivar ($3 billion) fiscal contribution to the government.
Average production of crude oil and condensates over the year was 14 percent above 1995 at 905,000 bpd, and sales of crude and products amounted to 893,000 bpd.

The subsidiary of Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said exploration activity also saw a marked increase during the year, recording 1,506 kilometers of 2D seismic study -- a ten-year record high -- and 346 kilometers of 3D work. It said there were important new exploration prospects in northern Anzoategui, eastern Barinas and Apure states.

Total crude reserves rose by 789 million barrels in 1996, with discoveries in Barinas, northern Anzoategui and Monagas, but the company did not give a total reserves figure. It said it was still evaluating a gas deposit in the Flanco Surandino region.
Refined products output grew by 2.7 percent to 343,000 bpd, and reformulated gasoline production reached 5,000 bpd.
The company said it built two compressor stations in northern Monagas as part of a gas reinjection project intended to boost potential recoverable reserves at the field by 558 million barrels.

Corpoven's operating agreements involving private capital hiked output by 61 percent to 51,000 bpd. The five projects together exceeded forecasts, largely due output growth at the Oritupano-Leona field, operated by Perez Companc, and the Quiamare-La Ceiba block operated by Astra and Tecpetrol.
